text:
Alex M: Quick Q — I'm about to land a TF change to grant our ingest IRSA role decrypt on the legacy KMS key (arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:012345678901:key/abcd-legacy). Thinking between aws_kms_grant vs editing the key policy. Any ordering pitfalls? Plan: create grant, then annotate k8s SA and rollout. Worried pods will try to decrypt before the grant propagates. Also want to scope with encryption context. Thoughts?

Mira S: I'd go aws_kms_grant — smaller blast radius than key policy. Add an encryption_context_subset constraint (e.g., {service="vectorizer"}) so it's scoped. And ensure grantee_principal is the IAM role ARN that IRSA creates. Avoid altering key policy unless you need cross-account broad access.

Dan R: FYI we've hit the race where annotation lands and pods restart before the grant exists — kube controller will push tokens immediately. Two mitigations: 1) make the grant exist first (obvious), 2) add a short readiness probe in the pod that retries decrypt, or 3) have TF wait and validate by attempting a small decrypt with a test ciphertext (null_resource + local-exec with retry).

Mira S: Example TF snippet that worked for us:
```hcl
data "aws_kms_key" "legacy" {
  key_id = "alias/legacy-key"
}

resource "aws_iam_role" "ingest_irsa" {
  name = "ingest-irsa-role"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_assume.json
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "ingest_grant" {
  name               = "ingest-irsa-${substr(aws_iam_role.ingest_irsa.name, 0, 8)}"
  key_id             = data.aws_kms_key.legacy.id
  grantee_principal  = aws_iam_role.ingest_irsa.arn
  operations         = ["Encrypt", "Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
  constraints {
    encryption_context_subset = {
      service = "vectorizer"
    }
  }
  depends_on = [aws_iam_role.ingest_irsa]
}
```

Dan R: If you want a verification step in TF, do a null_resource with local-exec that runs a small retry loop: `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://test.enc --key-id ${data.aws_kms_key.legacy.key_id}`. We scripted retries (30s total) and only proceeded if decrypt returned ok. Not super pretty but effective for infra changes.

Priya K: Alternative: make the application tolerant — start up and if decrypt fails, fall back to local cache or wait a few seconds then retry. That's often simpler than adding waits in TF. But for migration rollouts where pods are recreated immediately, TF wait+check is safe.

Alex M: Good points. I'll prefer aws_kms_grant + encryption_context_subset + a null_resource check. Will also add a note in the PR about the rollback: remove grant and re-deploy pods.

Mira S: One more: remember to use predictable grant names and tag them so we can identify and revoke easily later. Also add to the key's audit doc the principal ARN and the tf resource address. :+1:

deploy-bot: Runbook: KMS grant & IRSA migration — https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kms-irsa-migration (steps: create grant, validate decrypt, annotate SA, rollout, monitor logs).

Alex M: Thanks everyone — dropping the PR in a few mins. Will link the null_resource test and the test ciphertext generation steps. :eyes: 

Dan R: Happy to review the PR. If you want, I can add the retry script snippet I used.

Priya K: Ping me after deploy and I'll run a quick smoke against staging vectorizer.

Alex M: Awesome, will do.
